passages.text: Some say, “If he did not want them to exist, they would not exist, but would have been destroyed.” I too say that this certainly will happen when everyone has displayed his own choice toward him; then the present world will be changed. Yet even if you wanted him to act in this way, so that none of the things worshiped existed, tell us: which existing thing have you not worshiped? Do not some of you worship the sun, others the moon, others water, others earth, others mountains, others plants, others seeds, and others even a human being, as in Egypt? Then God would have had to leave nothing, not even us, so that there would be neither anything worshiped nor anyone worshiping. Truly, this is what the terrible serpent lurking within you wants to happen; he does not spare you. But it will not be so. For the thing worshiped commits no sin: it suffers violence at the hands of the person who wants to worship it. Even if all human beings judge unjustly, God does not. For it is not just for the one who suffers and the one who inflicts it to receive the same punishment—unless the former himself willingly accepts the honor belonging to the one who alone is most worthy of honor.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὴν αὐτῶν πρὸς αὐτὸν δείξωσιν προαίρεσιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: has displayed his own choice toward him
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains human choice and its orientation toward God without inserting a doctrine of predestination.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐκτὸς εἰ μὴ αὐτὸς ἑκὼν ἀναδέξηται τὴν τοῦ μόνου τιμιωτάτου τιμήν.
lexical_decisions.chosen: unless the former himself willingly accepts the honor belonging to the one who alone is most worthy of honor
lexical_decisions.rationale: The exception concerns a recipient of worship willingly accepting divine honor. No named example is added.

passages.text: “But,” someone says, “the worshipers themselves ought to be destroyed by the true God, so that no one else does this.” But you are not wiser than God, so as to offer him advice as someone more intelligent. He knows what he is doing. For he is patient with all who live in impiety, like a merciful father who loves humanity, knowing that even impious people become reverent. Many of the very people who revere shameful and insensible things have become clear-minded, stopped revering them and sinning, and taken refuge in the true God; through prayers and good deeds they have been saved.

lexical_decisions.rationale: Uses the POB clear-minded rendering for awakening from religious error, not an exclusively literal sobriety claim.

lexical_decisions.chosen: through prayers and good deeds they have been saved
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the author’s explicit linkage of salvation, prayers, and good deeds without imposing a denominational explanation.

passages.text: “But from the beginning he ought to have made us not even think about such things at all.” In saying this, you do not know what freedom of choice is or how it is possible to be truly good. For the person who is good by his own choice is truly good; the person made good by someone else’s compulsion is not truly so, because he is not what he is by his own choice. Since each person’s freedom produces what is truly good and reveals what is truly evil, God has arranged, through the circumstances, for becoming an enemy or a friend to lie within each person. “No,” someone says, “rather, he himself makes us think everything that we think.” Stop! What further blasphemy are you speaking when you say this? For if everything we think is put into effect in us by him, you are calling him the cause of sexual immoralities, shameless acts, greed, and every blasphemy. Stop speaking ill of him, you who ought to speak well of him and assign him every honor. And do not say, “God does not claim honor.” Even if he claims nothing, we still ought, with an eye to what is just, to repay with a thankful voice the one who has benefited us in every way.

lexical_decisions.rationale: Literally self-determination or being in one’s own power; the paragraph explicitly contrasts personal choice and external compulsion.
ὑποθέσεις can denote situations, underlying conditions, or proposed matters; circumstances fits the arrangements in which choice operates without specifying their exact mechanism.
Preserves distinct vice categories without embellishing sexual content or reducing all three to a generic evil.

passages.text: “But,” someone says, “we do better by thanking him and everyone else together.” In saying this, you do not know the plot against you. For suppose many physicians promise to treat one sick person but can do nothing, while one who really can heal does not administer his remedy, reasoning that if he heals the patient, others will take the credit. In the same way, when God is esteemed along with many who can do nothing, he does not bestow benefits. “What then?” someone says. “Is God indignant about this, if someone else gets the credit when he heals?” I say that even if he is not indignant, he still does not wish to become an accomplice in deception. For when he does good, the idol that has done nothing is also confirmed as having power. I too say that if the person infatuated with insensible things were not harmed in his nature, perhaps God would have put up even with this. So become clear-minded for the sake of salvation and think what is reasonable. For God, being without need, himself needs nothing and is not harmed. It is we who benefit or are harmed. Just as Caesar is neither harmed when he is reviled nor benefited when he is thanked, but safety belongs to the one who thanks him and destruction to the one who reviles him, so those who speak well of God do not benefit him at all but save themselves. Likewise, those who blaspheme do him no injury but are themselves destroyed.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰ μὴ φυσικῶς ἠδίκητο πρὸς ἀναίσθητα ἐπτοημένος, ἴσως ἂν καὶ τοῦτο ὑπομεμενήκει
lexical_decisions.chosen: if the person infatuated with insensible things were not harmed in his nature, perhaps God would have put up even with this
lexical_decisions.rationale: The subject of being harmed and infatuated is understood as the worshiper, while the subject of putting up with this is God, who immediately afterward is explicitly said not to suffer harm. φυσικῶς can also mean naturally. The Greek leaves these subjects implicit, so this contextual subject differentiation is disclosed.
Retains the imperial name/title without identifying a particular emperor.

passages.text: “But,” someone says, “it is not the same with a human being and God.” I agree that it is not the same. For the punishment is greater for having shown irreverence toward one who is greater, and less for the one who has sinned against someone lesser. Thus, just as God is greater than all, the person who has shown irreverence toward him will undergo greater punishment for having sinned against someone greater. It is not that God retaliates with his own hand; rather, all creation is indignant at this and pursues the offender by its nature. For neither will the sun give the blasphemer light, nor the earth its fruits, nor a spring its water, nor the ruler established in Hades give the soul there rest, since even now, while the world’s allotted term still stands, all creation shares in the indignation. Therefore neither does heaven provide rain in full nor the earth its fruits, and most people are consequently brought to ruin. Even the air itself, inflamed with anger, changes to act as a pestilence. Yet whatever good things we enjoy, he compels creation by his mercy to act with love toward us. This is how all creation is angry with you who dishonor the maker of all.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐκ ἐν ᾅδῃ τῇ ψυχῇ ὁ ἐκεῖ καθεστὼς ἄρχων τὴν ἀνάπαυσιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: nor the ruler established in Hades give the soul there rest
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains Hades as the source’s named realm; it is not replaced by a later, more specific doctrine of hell.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐπὶ τῆς τοῦ κόσμου προθεσμίας ὑφεστώσης
lexical_decisions.chosen: while the world’s allotted term still stands
lexical_decisions.rationale: The stated time-limit belongs to the world; the text does not supply its length.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῷ αὐτοῦ ἐλέῳ εἰς τὴν ἡμετέραν φιλανθρωπίαν βιάζεται τὴν κτίσιν.
lexical_decisions.chosen: he compels creation by his mercy to act with love toward us
lexical_decisions.rationale: The reflexive/possessive references are retained contextually: God compels creation toward humane treatment of us. The active force of βιάζεται is not softened into permission.
